arguments.report:
## Root cause

The reported example `dayjs('2020-08-06T03:48:10.258Z').tz('Asia/Tokyo')` goes through `proto.tz` (the instance method), **not** `tzOffset`/`d.tz`. In `src/plugin/timezone/index.js`:

```js
const target = this.toDate().toLocaleString('en-US', { timeZone: timezone })
const diff = (this.toDate() - new Date(target)) / 1000 / 60
return d(target).utcOffset(localUtcOffset - diff, true)
```

`this.toDate()` keeps the `.258` ms, but `toLocaleString` omits milliseconds, so `new Date(target)` has ms = 0. The subtraction therefore yields a **fractional-minute** diff (`-539.9956999999999`). With `keepLocalTime = true`, `utcOffset()` stores that raw fractional value in `$offset` (`539.9957...`), and `format('Z')` floors it → `+08:59`. With a whole second the diff is an exact integer, hence no bug.

(`tzOffset` itself is fine: it truncates `asTS` to whole seconds via `asTS -= asTS % 1000`, so it never returns a fractional minute. The bug is in `proto.tz`'s diff computation.)

## Change (src/plugin/timezone/index.js, minimal & targeted — only `proto.tz`)

```diff
+import { MS } from '../../constant'
+
 const typeToPos = {
...
   proto.tz = function (timezone) {
     const target = this.toDate().toLocaleString('en-US', { timeZone: timezone })
-    const diff = (this.toDate() - new Date(target)) / 1000 / 60
-    return d(target).utcOffset(localUtcOffset - diff, true)
+    const diff = Math.round((this.toDate() - new Date(target)) / 1000 / 60)
+    return d(target).$set(MS, this.$ms).utcOffset(localUtcOffset - diff, true)
   }
```

- `Math.round` makes the offset a clean whole number of minutes.
- `$set(MS, this.$ms)` is required to keep the milliseconds: previously the ms survived only accidentally via the fractional offset in `valueOf()`; rounding alone would have dropped them (`...258` → `...000`). This makes `valueOf()`, `format('SSS')` and the offset all consistent with moment.

`src/plugin/weekYear/index.js` only handled ONE side of the week-year boundary: "week 1 falling in December → next year". It had no symmetric case for "last week (52/53) falling in January → previous year".

`weekOfYear` itself is correct: for en-gb (`weekStart:1`, `yearStart:4`, i.e. ISO dow=1/doy=4), `dayjs('2021-01-01').week()` returns `53` (verified equal to `moment(...).week()`), because Jan 1–3 2021 (Fri–Sun) belong to ISO week 53 of 2020.      }
+    if (month === 0 && weekOfYear >= 52) {

+    }

## Root cause

`src/plugin/customParseFormat/index.js` hard-coded English AM/PM for the `A`/`a` tokens:

```js
const matchUpperCaseAMPM = /[AP]M/
const matchLowerCaseAMPM = /[ap]m/
...
A: [matchUpperCaseAMPM, function (input) { this.afternoon = input === 'PM' }],
a: [matchLowerCaseAMPM, function (input) { this.afternoon = input === 'pm' }],
```

The format side (`src/index.js` `format()`, lines 299–322) calls the locale's `meridiem(hour, minute, isLowercase)` if present. `zh-cn`'s `meridiem` returns `'凌晨'/'早上'/'上午'/'中午'/'下午'/'晚上'` (src/locale/zh-cn.js:48), so `dayjs(...).locale('zh-cn').format('YYYY年M月D日Ah点mm分ss秒')` produced e.g. `2018年5月2日凌晨1点02分03秒`. On parse, the `A` regex `/[AP]M/` could not match `凌晨`, `regex.exec(part)` returned `null`, `match[0]` threw, and the catch in `parseFormattedInput` returned `new Date('')` → Invalid Date. The same bug affects any locale with a non-English `meridiem` (ja, ko, br, zh).

## Fix (only file touched: `src/plugin/customParseFormat/index.js`)

## Root cause
In `src/plugin/duration/index.js`, the `unitToMS` lookup table (lines 8–16) had no `milliseconds` entry. The constructor does `wrapper(input * unitToMS[prettyUnit(unit)], this)` (line 33), and `prettyUnit` = `` `${$u.p(unit)}s` `` normalizes `'ms'` → `'millisecond'` → `'milliseconds'`. So `unitToMS.milliseconds` was `undefined`, making `1 * undefined === NaN`; the resulting NaN duration serialized as `'P0D'`. The no-unit path and other units were unaffected, and `as('ms')`/object-`ms` worked only because those code paths use a `|| 1` fallback (`calMilliseconds` line 62, `as` line 108) that the two-argument constructor path lacks. `add(1, 'ms')` was broken for the same reason (line 127).

   minutes: MILLISECONDS_A_MINUTE,
   seconds: MILLISECONDS_A_SECOND,
+  milliseconds: 1,
